title: Human Resource System Performance, Perceived Process Quality, and Risk-Related Outcomes in Organizational Systems: Evidence from the European Social Survey
content: This study examines the relationships between human resource system performance, perceived process quality, and risk-related outcomes within an organizational systems framework. Using data from 750 respondents from the European Social Survey, Round 9, the study applies correlation, regression, mediation, and exploratory factor analyses. Since the dataset does not include direct organizational-level measures of formal HR systems, process quality, or corporate risk, a perception-based proxy approach is adopted. The findings indicate that human-resource-related indicators are significantly associated with perceived system stability and risk-related organizational outcomes, with general satisfaction and work engagement emerging as the most consistent predictors. Mediation analysis suggests that perceived process quality and reliability partially mediate the association between human resource system performance and risk-related outcomes. Exploratory factor analysis indicates a broadly interpretable two-dimensional structure of the examined indicators. The study contributes to systems-oriented organizational research by showing how human-resource-related conditions, perceived process quality, and risk-related outcomes may be interconnected within broader organizational systems. The findings offer practical implications for strengthening process reliability, organizational resilience, and risk-oriented management.
